chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mansur al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm in a man enjoying [being married to] two sisters." This is not contradictory to what we have previously stated, because the apparent meaning of the report does not indicate that he may enjoy both sisters simultaneously or in two distinct states. If this is not apparent in its text, we interpret it to mean that it is permissible for him to contract marriage with each one after the other. We have previously presented the report which includes that the one being enjoyed [the first wife], when her waiting period expires, her husband may not enjoy her sister until her waiting period expires. This is indicative of what we said and alerts to the fact that he did not intend enjoying both sisters simultaneously. The ruling of female slaves is the same as that of free women regarding prohibition and combining two sisters in intercourse. The Verse indicates this according to what we have stated, and this is also confirmed by what was narrated.
ai.seo_question: Can a man be married to two sisters at the same time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction by distinguishing between simultaneous marriage (jam') and sequential temporary marriage (tamattu'), noting that the hadith permits the latter. He reinforces this by citing the parallel ruling for female slaves (mawali) and linking it to the Quranic prohibition, thereby clarifying that the restriction applies to the act of enjoyment rather than the contract itself.
